chapter: The Legends of Jazz and life on the road
title: Audiences in the South today
summary: Audiences in the South are mixed and of all ages, and young people go for their music.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Since the group of dancers and the girl singer have been added to the Legends, have you played any places down South, and what might be the response?
What kinds of people do you find in your audiences down South now, any age group?
Teens up to in the eighties and nineties, grandmas and great grandmas.
I'm surprised at the youngsters who go for our music. I've seen teenage girls, even black teenage girls, come up to me and say you're so wonderful, I just want to kiss you.
Of course the audiences now are mixed, even in the South.
Integrated audience, yeah. A far cry from fifty years ago.
